title: evaluation-calibration-framework-and-llm-as-judge-protocol
creator: Alex Novak
description:
Background:
Redwood's regression monitoring currently compares aggregate eval scores before/after model or config changes, but teams have observed noisy signals and inconsistent actionability when small configuration tweaks (batch size, quantization profile, temperature) cause subtle quality drift. This ticket defines a repeatable benchmarking and scoring methodology that uses LLM-as-judge judgements + calibrated human anchors to produce stable, explainable regression signals gated for rollout.

Goals: 
- Create an evaluation calibration framework that reduces false positives and false negatives for quality regressions triggered by model/config changes.
- Standardize a rubric and LLM-judge protocol so different teams can reproduce scores across workloads.
- Define gating thresholds and statistical tests for automatic rollout blocks and alerts.
- Integrate calibrated scores into Console's rollout dashboard and the Optimize recommendations pipeline.

Proposal summary: 
1) Rubric taxonomy: we will standardize a three-layer rubric applicable across text-generation use cases: 
   - Coherence: is response on-topic and logically consistent? (binary + severity)
   - Correctness/faithfulness: factual errors or hallucinations (0-3 severity buckets)
   - Safety/toxicity: flagged via safety classifiers and hand-annotated examples (binary + contextual severity)
   - Format/structured-output adherence: for function-calling or JSON output (pass/fail + error class)

2) LLM-as-judge protocol: 
   - Use a curated judge model (e.g., open-model-judge-v1) with fixed temperature=0 and deterministic sampling.
   - Prompt template includes rubric definitions, clear examples (positive/negative), and a calibration section that provides 10 anchor examples with human labels.
   - Judge returns: discrete label per rubric axis, numeric confidence score (0-1), and a short rationale (1-2 sentences).

3) Calibration & anchoring: 
   - Collect a 300-example anchor set per workload class (chat, summarization, code-generation, instruction-following) with multi-rater human labels.
   - Compute judge-to-human calibration mapping (isotonic regression) to convert judge confidence to calibrated probability.
   - Store per-workload calibration curves; re-run calibration whenever the judge model or significant rubric changes occur.

4) Sampling & statistical testing: 
   - For a given model/config change, sample N=1000 inputs from the production-weighted traffic distribution (min N=300 for low-volume).
   - Compute per-axis paired differences and run bootstrap confidence intervals + permutation tests to estimate p-values.
   - Apply multiple-testing correction across axes (Benjamini-Hochberg) and require both statistically significant degradation (p_adj < 0.05) and effect size threshold (e.g., absolute calibrated-prob delta > 0.03) to trigger an auto-block.

5) Explainability & triage: 
   - For each detected regression, return: top 20 examples with highest drop in calibrated score, judge rationales, token-level diffs and per-example confidence.
   - Provide recommended mitigations: rollback, quantization profile change, targeted prompt/patching, or fine-grained A/B.

6) Rollout gating & Console integration: 
   - Automatic gating rules evaluate canary vs baseline for new rollout: require no axis with significant degradation (per rule above) for canary size <= 5%. For larger canary sizes (>5%) require additional manual sign-off.
   - Add a "Calibration" panel in Console showing judge-to-human calibration curves, anchor set stats, and historical false-positive rate.

Acceptance criteria: 
- PM/Eng agree on the rubric axes and anchor dataset size for 3 workload classes.
- A reproducible LLM-as-judge prompt + exemplar set is checked in to the evals repo and passes CI.
- Calibration pipeline computes judge->human mapping and produces a dashboard plot.
- Automated test detects a synthetic regression in a staged test (pipeline must flag and provide top-20 examples).
- Console shows gating status and per-axis p-values for a sample canary run.

Implementation notes / technical constraints: 
- Judge model must be pinned in the model catalog for reproducibility. If we upgrade judge model, mark previous calibration as deprecated.
- Calibration relies on a human-labeled anchor; we will coordinate with Solutions and Research to collect anchors. Anchors must be storeable in S3 with metadata.
- Compute costs: running judge over 1000 examples x multi-axis will be billed to the evals budget; optimize by batching and using cached judge outputs where possible.

Data handling & privacy: 
- Anchors may contain redacted PII; follow Privacy policy and ensure anchors are labeled in private S3 buckets with access controls.
- Audit logs of judge decisions and human labels must be retained 90 days for investigations, then archived.

Risks: 
- LLM-judge may inherit biases; calibration lowers but does not eliminate this risk. We'll require periodic human audits of judge outputs.
- Overfitting to anchor set—use cross-validation and rotating anchor samples to reduce brittleness.

Timeline & milestones: 
- Week 1 (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-16): finalize rubric and anchor collection plan; implement judge prompt template.
- Week 2: implement calibration pipeline and basic CI; run calibration with initial anchor.
- Week 3: integrate statistical testing and produce automated regression detection on staged testbed.
- Week 4: Console integration (panel + gating rule) and final sign-offs.

Open questions: 
- Which judge model to pin as "canonical" for Q2? (Research to propose candidate models.)
- Minimum anchor size per niche workload (code generation is likely to need more than 300).
- How to surface judge rationales in Console without leaking prompt examples? (Design/Legal input required.)
